rules.trigger: Linux aarch64 AND (/etc/dgx-release DGX_NAME="DGX Spark" OR nvidia-smi name "NVIDIA GB10" OR lspci [10de:2e12] OR DMI product_name NVIDIA_DGX_Spark)
rules.evidence_template: GB10 platform: {vendor} {model} ({fe_or_oem}); GPU {gpu} CC {cc}; kernel {kernel}; DGX OS {swbuild} / OTA {ota}.
rules.why_it_matters: Enables unified-memory suppressions and DGX OS pairing rules; OEM units lag NVIDIA OTAs.
next_steps: No action; memory comes from /proc/meminfo, nvidia-smi memory fields are expected to be [N/A].

rules.trigger: Windows host ARM64 AND PNPDeviceID PCI\VEN_10DE&DEV_2E03|2E06 (or Name contains "RTX Spark")
rules.evidence_template: RTX Spark N1X ({cores}-core, DEV_{devid}), Windows build {build} ARM64, {oem_model}, pool {ram_gib} GiB.
rules.why_it_matters: Unified memory and Windows-on-Arm change what nvidia-smi, AdapterRAM (uint32) and CUDA report.
next_steps: Report total RAM as the GPU pool; record driver version and INF.

rules.trigger: aarch64 AND nvidia-smi name contains GH200/GB200/GB300 AND memory.total numeric
rules.evidence_template: {gpu}, {vram_mib} MiB HBM, CC {cc}, NUMA nodes {numa}.
rules.why_it_matters: Coherent memory but real HBM, ECC, BMC; GB10 suppressions must not apply.
next_steps: Apply standard datacenter rules.

rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND (memory.total/used/free == [N/A] OR table Memory-Usage == "Not Supported")
rules.evidence_template: nvidia-smi memory '{value}' on {gpu} is expected on unified-memory iGPUs. Pool: MemTotal {total_gib} GiB (128 GB = 119.2 GiB minus 2-4 GB display reserve), MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB, swap {swap_gib} GiB. Fan, power limit, memory clock and PCIe gen/width are also [N/A] or misreported.
rules.why_it_matters: Suppresses low-vram, fan, power-limit and PCIe false alarms; cudaMemGetInfo also under-reports.
next_steps: Use /proc/meminfo MemAvailable (+SwapFree), free -h 'available' or the DGX Dashboard (http://localhost:11000).

rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND (MemAvailable < 16 GiB with a GPU process; CRIT < 8 GiB) OR /proc/pressure/memory full avg10 > 0.1
rules.evidence_template: MemAvailable {avail_gib} of {total_gib} GiB; PSI full avg10 {psi}; GPU processes {n}.
rules.why_it_matters: GPU exhaustion is system RAM exhaustion: OOM killer, frozen SSH or log-less hard reset.
next_steps: Lower vLLM --gpu-memory-utilization (<= 0.85), --max-model-len, --max-num-seqs; stop other model servers; sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'.

rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND SwapTotal-SwapFree > 0 (or zram in use) while GPU utilization > 0
rules.evidence_template: Swap in use: {used_gib} of {total_gib} GiB ({device}); vm.swappiness={sw}. GB10: 6.7 GiB swapped cost 43% tok/s, 13 GiB 95%.
rules.why_it_matters: Paging the shared pool collapses decode throughput and can hang the box.
next_steps: Reduce footprint; inference hosts: sudo swapoff -a and comment swap out of /etc/fstab; otherwise vm.swappiness=1.

rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND MemFree < 4 GiB AND MemAvailable - MemFree > 20 GiB
rules.evidence_template: MemFree {free_gib} GiB but MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB: {cache_gib} GiB page cache competes with the GPU.
rules.why_it_matters: NVIDIA's documented cause of 'memory issues even though within capacity'.
next_steps: sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' then restart the application.

rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND kernel log 'Out of memory: Killed process' (WARN) or 'NVRM: nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY]' (CRIT)
rules.evidence_template: {n_oom} OOM-killer events (last {comm}), {n_nvrm} NVRM NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY events; MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB, swap used {swap_gib} GiB.
rules.why_it_matters: On GB10 these RM failures preceded log-less hard resets with no Xid trail.
next_steps: Keep >= 8-16 GiB headroom; lower utilization fractions; driver >= 580.159.03 via the Dashboard; systemd-run -p MemoryMax for heavy jobs.

rules.trigger: lspci [10de:2e12] AND nvidia-smi 'No devices were found' AND dmesg 'Timeout after 6s of waiting for RPC response from GPU0 GSP' / 'ksec2PrepareBootCommands_GB20B: SEC2 secure boot partition timed out' / 'RmInitAdapter: Cannot initialize GSP firmware RM' / Xid 119
rules.evidence_template: GPU at 000f:01:00.0 but nvidia-smi 'No devices were found'; dmesg '{line}'; nvidia-driver-580-open {drv}, nvidia-firmware-580 {fw}, OTA {ota}, kernel {kernel}.
rules.why_it_matters: Driver and GSP firmware are paired per OTA; a plain apt upgrade (580.173.02 on OTA2607 = 580.159.03) leaves the GPU unbootable.
next_steps: sudo nvidia-spark-ota-check summary; re-run the DGX Dashboard update (or apt dist-upgrade + fwupdmgr upgrade + reboot, AC unplugged 30 s after firmware); if stuck, downgrade to the paired driver, apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-580-open, collect nvidia-bug-report.sh.

rules.trigger: DGX OS AND (nvidia-spark-ota-check torn > 0 OR failed list non-empty OR nvidia-driver-580-open version != nvidia-firmware-580-* version OR linux-modules-nvidia-580-open-$(uname -r) missing)
rules.evidence_template: OTA {name} torn={torn}, failed {failed}; driver pkg {drv} vs firmware pkg {fw}; modules for {kernel}: {state}.
rules.why_it_matters: noble-updates ships newer 580 drivers before the OTA pairs them: GSP failure at next boot or a looping Dashboard update.
next_steps: Prefer Dashboard updates; if the same update keeps re-appearing: sudo apt install nvidia-firmware-580-<expected-version> and reboot.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND driver major < 580 or nvidia-smi CUDA Version 12.x
rules.evidence_template: Driver {driver} / CUDA {cuda}; GB10 requires R580 open modules and CUDA 13 (signature: ~5 W, 0% util, power limit N/A).
rules.why_it_matters: sm_121 is unsupported by pre-580 drivers; workloads silently run on CPU.
next_steps: Update via Dashboard or apt dist-upgrade + fwupdmgr upgrade + reboot; reimage if a manual install caused it.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND driver major in {590, 595}
rules.evidence_template: Driver {driver}: NVIDIA (2026-06) 'Driver 595 is not yet supported on DGX Spark'; 590.48.01 leaked ~93 GB after process exit.
rules.why_it_matters: Outside NVIDIA validation; breaks OTA pairing.
next_steps: Return to the OTA-paired 580.x via the Dashboard.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND dpkg has nvidia-driver-*-server, nvidia-dkms-*, nvidia-fabricmanager-*, nvidia-nvswitch-*, a non-'-open' driver or one without the -0ubuntu0.24.04 suffix; or nvidia-smi 'NVIDIA-GB10 not supported'
rules.evidence_template: Installed {pkgs}; expected nvidia-driver-580-open + nvidia-firmware-580-<ver> + linux-modules-nvidia-580-open-<kernel>. nvidia-smi '{err}'.
rules.why_it_matters: No NVSwitch on Spark, Secure Boot rejects DKMS modules; NVIDIA's remedy is a reimage.
next_steps: Remove foreign packages and reinstall the image driver set, or reimage (docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgx-spark/system-recovery.html).

rules.trigger: GB10 AND driver 580.x < 580.173.02 (INFO); WARN when logs contain 'CUDNN_FE failure 11: CUDNN_BACKEND_API_FAILED' or 'CUBLAS failure 14: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR'
rules.evidence_template: Driver {driver}; 580.173.02 fixed deterministic cuDNN/cuBLAS internal errors under batch load. Log '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Batch inference crashes; the fix must arrive via a pairing OTA, not plain apt.
next_steps: Update through the DGX Dashboard when it offers >= 580.173.02; do not pull it from apt ahead of the OTA.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND uname -r !~ ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+-\d+-nvidia$
rules.evidence_template: Kernel {kernel}; DGX Spark expects Canonical's linux-nvidia flavour (6.14.0-NNNN-nvidia / 6.17.0-NNNN-nvidia).
rules.why_it_matters: Generic kernels lack r8127, mt7925e, GB10 patches and signed NVIDIA modules.
next_steps: Boot the -nvidia kernel or sudo apt install linux-nvidia-hwe-24.04.

rules.trigger: DGX OS AND (DGX_OTA_VERSION < 7.5.0 OR kernel < 6.17 OR driver < 580.159.03)
rules.evidence_template: OTA {ota} ({date}), kernel {kernel}, driver {driver}; current FE stack DGX OS 7.5.0 / 580.159.03 / CUDA 13.0.2 / kernel 6.17.
rules.why_it_matters: Older OTAs: 6.14 mmap regression, Vulkan broken on 580.95.05, CX-7 power fixes, OOM handling (580.159.03).
next_steps: Update via DGX Dashboard (Settings > Updates); OEM units via the OEM channel.

rules.trigger: DGX OS AND (dgx-dashboard.service or dgx-dashboard-admin.service inactive OR 127.0.0.1:11000 closed OR fwupd.service failed / 'libfwupd version X does not match daemon Y' OR >3 lingering check_ota_status.py)
rules.evidence_template: dgx-dashboard {s1}, dgx-dashboard-admin {s2}, port 11000 {open}, fwupd {fw} ('{err}'), {n} stuck check_ota_status.py.
rules.why_it_matters: The Dashboard is the primary update path; a hung fwupd makes Updates spin forever.
next_steps: sudo apt install --only-upgrade fwupd && sudo systemctl restart fwupd dgx-dashboard dgx-dashboard-admin.

rules.trigger: fwupdmgr: FE EC < 0x03000508 (3.5.8), UEFI/SoC < 0x02009b0b (2.155.11), USB PD < 0x00000516 (0.5.22); ASUS GX10 BIOS < 0105; pending capsules; INFO when SBIOS is pre-production 5.36_0ACUM018
rules.evidence_template: EC {ec}, UEFI/SoC {soc}, USB-PD {pd}, SBIOS {sbios} ({vendor}); latest FE 0x03000508 / 0x02009b0b / 0x00000516 (July 2026); pending {pending}.
rules.why_it_matters: 2026 firmware waves target USB-PD and EC stability; NVIDIA says current firmware fixed the power wedge for some users.
next_steps: sudo fwupdmgr refresh && sudo fwupdmgr get-upgrades (read-only); apply via your vendor channel, then cold power-cycle (PSU unplugged); check get-history 'Update State: Success'.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND utilization.gpu >= 90 AND clocks.sm < 1400 MHz (typically 611/650/721) AND power.draw < 40 W AND all clock event reasons Not Active
rules.evidence_template: Under load: {clk} MHz (max 3003), {util}%, {power} W, {temp} C, {pstate}; reasons Not Active; SW Power Capping counter {us} us. Healthy: ~2200-2480 MHz at 80-100 W.
rules.why_it_matters: USB-C PD controller wedged (~13-30 W safety mode): 3-5x slower, -lgc has no effect, warm reboot does not clear it; NVIDIA RMAs persistent cases.
next_steps: Cold drain: shut down, unplug PSU from wall AND unit, unplug all USB-C, hold power 30 s, wait 60 s, reconnect the supplied adapter only, re-test under load; update firmware via your vendor channel, cold-drain again, avoid suspend; if it recurs: nvidia-bug-report.sh and support/RMA.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND journalctl -b -1 ends without shutdown markers ('Reached target Power-Off', 'reboot: Power down') AND no panic/OOM/Xid/thermal lines AND /sys/fs/pstore empty
rules.evidence_template: {n} unclean power-offs in {days} days; last line of boot -1 '{line}'; pstore empty; max SM clock {max_clock}; EC {ec}, SBIOS {sbios}.
rules.why_it_matters: EC/PSU cuts power under ~90 W sustained load faster than the kernel logs; NVIDIA is investigating and RMAs fieldiag PowerStress failures (MODS-020000610139).
next_steps: Supplied 240 W adapter direct to the wall, unstack, ambient 5-30 C, update firmware, cold power-cycle; reduce memory over-commit (same signature); community mitigation (manual, never applied by NVCheckup): sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 300,2200 (revert -rgc); fieldiag: sudo apt install dgx-spark-fieldiag; sudo init 3; sudo /opt/nvidia/dgx-spark-fieldiag/partnerdiag --field.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND any acpitz zone >= 93000 mC, or SW/HW Thermal Slowdown counters > 0 below the thermal-throttling thresholds
rules.evidence_template: ACPI zones {zones} (max {mc} mC) vs GPU {gpu_temp} C; slowdown counters SW {sw} / HW {hw} us; fan telemetry unavailable (EC); EC {ec}.
rules.why_it_matters: The package sensor runs up to 20 C above the GPU reading; 96-97 C zones with quiet fans precede hard power-offs.
next_steps: Improve airflow; check EC level (fwupdmgr get-devices); OEM units contact the OEM; fieldiag if it persists.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND (gb10-clock-cap.service exists OR 'Applications Clocks Setting: Active' OR locked max SM clock < 3003 MHz)
rules.evidence_template: Clocks locked to {min}-{max} MHz (hardware max 3003) via {source}; ~5-10% cost.
rules.why_it_matters: Explains lower clocks so they are not mistaken for throttling; does not fix the PD wedge.
next_steps: No action if intentional; remove with sudo nvidia-smi -rgc.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND journal 'PM: suspend entry (s2idle)' AND ('WARNING: ... at nvidia/nv.c:4784 nv_set_system_power_state' OR nvidia-suspend.service failed); also headless units whose GDM greeter sleep-inactive-ac-type != 'nothing'
rules.evidence_template: {n} suspend attempts; driver {driver} logged nv_set_system_power_state warning / nvidia-suspend.service failed; GDM greeter policy {policy}.
rules.why_it_matters: Suspend is disabled by default on Spark and s2idle does not complete; resume triggers the PD wedge; headless boxes suspend from the login screen and drop Wi-Fi.
next_steps: Keep suspend off (GNOME Automatic Suspend Off; systemctl mask sleep.target suspend.target; sudo -u gdm dbus-run-session gsettings set org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power sleep-inactive-ac-type 'nothing'); re-test clocks after any suspend.

rules.trigger: --include-logs AND dmesg 'mlx5_core ... Detected insufficient power on the PCIe slot (27W)' or correctable AER on the ConnectX-7
rules.evidence_template: dmesg '{line}': benign per NVIDIA moderators (no slot power limit advertised).
rules.why_it_matters: Prevents a false power fault; only fatal AER or a ~13 Gb/s link matters.
next_steps: Ignore unless gb10-pd-power-wedge or cx7-link-speed-degraded also fires.

rules.trigger: torch.version.cuda 12.x / wheel tag +cu12x, or import error 'libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file' / 'libnvrtc.so.12', on a CUDA 13-only host
rules.evidence_template: {package} {version} is built for CUDA {pkg_cuda}; host has only CUDA {host_cuda} ({missing_lib} absent).
rules.why_it_matters: The package cannot import or falls back to CPU; the most common GB10 setup failure.
next_steps: pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130; vLLM +cu130 aarch64 wheel or https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cu130; SGLang lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130; remove nvidia-*-cu12 packages.

rules.trigger: torch probe stderr 'Found GPU0 NVIDIA GB10 which is of cuda capability 12.1. Minimum and Maximum cuda capability supported by this version of PyTorch is (8.0) - (12.0)' or arch list has sm_120 but not sm_121
rules.evidence_template: PyTorch {version} (CUDA {torch_cuda}) warns about capability 12.1; arch list {arch_list}. sm_120 SASS runs on sm_121.
rules.why_it_matters: Stops users rebuilding PyTorch for sm_121 or blaming the warning for unrelated failures.
next_steps: No action; confirm torch.version.cuda starts with 13 and a matmul runs on cuda.

rules.trigger: CC 12.1 AND (logs 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device', 'kernel built for sm80-sm100, but running on sm121', 'cudaErrorSymbolNotFound', 'TRTLLMGenFusedMoE does not support SM120 and above' OR torch arch list lacks sm_120/sm_121/compute_120)
rules.evidence_template: {component} has no sm_120/sm_120f/sm_121a kernels: '{line}'. GB10/N1X are CC 12.1; sm_100 and sm_90 binaries never run here.
rules.why_it_matters: Kernel launches fail or fall back to slow generic paths (~4x slower decode measured).
next_steps: Use cu130 aarch64 wheels or NGC images with sm_121 (pytorch >= 25.10, vllm 26.xx, tensorrt-llm >= 1.2); rebuild with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1+PTX" / CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121a-real; verify cuobjdump --list-elf <lib.so> | grep -c sm_12.

rules.trigger: triton installed AND (bundled ptxas < 13.0 AND TRITON_PTXAS_PATH unset) OR logs "ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_121a' is not defined for option 'gpu-name'"
rules.evidence_template: Triton {tv} bundles ptxas {pv}; TRITON_PTXAS_PATH={val}; system ptxas {sys}. Error '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: torch.compile, FlashInfer/Triton attention and TRT-LLM NVFP4 kernels JIT at runtime and abort.
next_steps: export TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas (mpirun -x for TRT-LLM); TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1+PTX".

rules.trigger: aarch64 AND pip has flash_attn / vllm-flash-attn (or Transformers 'FlashAttention2 has been toggled on, but flash_attn is not installed')
rules.evidence_template: flash_attn {version} on aarch64: no official linux_aarch64+sm121 wheels exist.
rules.why_it_matters: Import errors break attn_implementation='flash_attention_2'; Blackwell guidance is SDPA.
next_steps: pip uninstall flash-attn; use attn_implementation="sdpa" or NGC bundled kernels; if required build from source with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.0" FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS="120".

rules.trigger: docker image inspect Architecture == amd64 on aarch64, or container logs 'exec format error'
rules.evidence_template: Image {image} is linux/amd64; host is linux/arm64.
rules.why_it_matters: The container cannot start and users blame the GPU/driver.
next_steps: Pull an arm64 tag (docker manifest inspect must list linux/arm64); check the DGX Spark Collection on NGC before pulling NIMs.

rules.trigger: images include nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch <= 25.09 (24.08-py3 is still on the DGX Spark NGC doc page), nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorflow (EOL after 25.02), lmsysorg/sglang:latest (cu12), or tensorrt-llm/release < 1.2
rules.evidence_template: {image} predates CUDA 13 / sm_121 (first CUDA 13 NGC PyTorch 25.08, GB10 kernels from 25.10, playbook baseline 25.11-py3).
rules.why_it_matters: nvidia-smi works inside but torch.cuda.is_available() is False or kernels fail.
next_steps: Use nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.11-py3+, nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05-py3, tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc13, lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130; pin tags.

rules.trigger: snap list docker succeeds, or error 'nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: load library failed: libnvidia-ml.so.1'
rules.evidence_template: Snap Docker {ver} installed; docker-ce {state}; error '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Snap-confined Docker cannot load host NVML; Spark expects docker-ce plus nv-docker-gpus/nv-docker-options.
next_steps: sudo snap remove docker; sudo apt install docker-ce docker-ce-cli docker-compose-plugin nv-docker-gpus nv-docker-options.

rules.trigger: daemon.json enables CDI AND no /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml or /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml (or logs 'no nvidia.com/gpu CDI spec is present on the host'); INFO variant when daemon.json lacks runtimes.nvidia ('unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia')
rules.evidence_template: Docker CDI {cdi}, nvidia.yaml {present}, runtimes {runtimes} (toolkit {ctk}); error '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Factory images (toolkit 1.19.0) shipped without the CDI spec unit; --gpus all works without the named runtime, compose files using runtime: nvidia do not.
next_steps: sudo nvidia-ctk cdi generate --output=/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml; sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker && sudo systemctl restart docker.

rules.trigger: onnxruntime importable AND 'CUDAExecutionProvider' not in get_available_providers() (both onnxruntime and onnxruntime-gpu installed, or PyPI CPU wheel on aarch64)
rules.evidence_template: Providers {providers}; onnxruntime={v1}, onnxruntime-gpu={v2}. No official onnxruntime-gpu aarch64 wheels; the CPU wheel overwrites a GPU build.
rules.why_it_matters: ONNX-backed pipelines run on CPU with no error.
next_steps: pip uninstall onnxruntime; install the sm_121 onnxruntime-gpu build or build ORT >= 1.24 with CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 and libcudnn9-cuda-13.

rules.trigger: kubectl present AND device plugin < v0.17.4 (DRA driver < v0.4.0, HAMi <= 2.7.1) or pod logs 'error getting device memory: Not Supported'
rules.evidence_template: {plugin} {version} on GB10: '{line}'; nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo returns NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED on unified memory.
rules.why_it_matters: Node advertises zero nvidia.com/gpu (CrashLoopBackOff); MPS also fails, only time-slicing works.
next_steps: Upgrade k8s-device-plugin >= v0.17.4 / dra-driver >= v0.4.0 / HAMi with preConfiguredDeviceMemory; do not rely on the gpu.memory label.

rules.trigger: GB10 AND no PCI 15b3 devices AND dmesg 'cx7-pcie-hotplug MTKP0001:00: Cable removal' or 'broken device, retraining non-functional downstream link at 2.5GT/s'; WARN variant when kernel is 6.17.0-1021-nvidia or 6.17.0-1029-nvidia even if the NIC is present
rules.evidence_template: ConnectX-7 not enumerated: {count} 15b3 devices; kernel {kernel}; dmesg '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: No 200 Gb/s link, RoCE or multi-node NCCL; 6.17.0-1021/1029-nvidia have a hotplug regression that drops the NIC 5-22 s after boot, retraining failures needed RMA.
next_steps: Cold power cycle with power and QSFP unplugged; on 6.17.0-1021/1029 pin linux-image-6.14.0-1015-nvidia + matching nvidia-580-open modules; persistent 'retraining failed' -> fieldiag and RMA.

rules.trigger: within one cage (functions .0 of PCI domains 0000 and 0002 = port 0; .1 = port 1) one twin ACTIVE and the other DOWN, or dmesg 'QSFP module not powered' / 'Cable unplugged'
rules.evidence_template: Port {port}: {twin_a} {state_a} but {twin_b} {state_b}; /etc/nvidia/cx7-hotplug-enabled {present}.
rules.why_it_matters: Each cage is two 100 Gb/s PCIe x4 twins; one twin down caps the link at ~100 Gb/s; the Jan-2026 hot-plug power file can keep lanes from training.
next_steps: Reseat an approved DAC (Amphenol NJAAKK-N911/NJAAKK0006, Luxshare LMTQF022-SD-R), reboot both nodes with the cable attached; if lanes never train: sudo rm -f /etc/nvidia/cx7-hotplug-enabled on both nodes and reboot.

rules.trigger: an Up CX-7 twin reports /sys/class/net/<if>/speed != 200000
rules.evidence_template: {iface} negotiated {speed} Mb/s; expected 200000; CX-7 firmware {fw}.
rules.why_it_matters: A 100G cable/switch port or firmware regression halves NCCL bandwidth; the ~13 Gb/s state needs a reboot with the cable attached or firmware + cold drain.
next_steps: Use a >= 200 Gb/s cable; fix switch ports at 200G, autoneg off, one L2 bridge, MTU 9000; sudo fwupdmgr get-upgrades.

rules.trigger: a CX-7 twin is ACTIVE/Up with no IPv4, or its address is not persisted in netplan/NM (INFO)
rules.evidence_template: {iface} ({rdma_dev}) Up at {speed} Mb/s; IPv4 {ip}; persistent config {persistent}.
rules.why_it_matters: NCCL and discover-sparks cannot use an unaddressed link; ip addr add is lost at reboot; with two cables all four twins need addresses.
next_steps: /etc/netplan/40-cx7.yaml (chmod 600) with dhcp4: no and a static address per twin; sudo netplan apply.

rules.trigger: both twins of a cage carry IPv4 addresses in the same subnet, or a twin is enslaved to a Linux bond
rules.evidence_template: {twin_a}={ip_a} and {twin_b}={ip_b} share {subnet}; bond {bond}.
rules.why_it_matters: Same-subnet or bonded twins break routing/ARP, RoCE reachability and NCCL autodiscovery ('Interfaces X and Y share the same subnet').
next_steps: One /24 per twin on both nodes (192.168.100.x / 192.168.101.x); remove bonds; list both twins in NCCL_IB_HCA.

rules.trigger: MTU differs between twins of a cage, or an addressed twin is 1500 while netplan/peer uses 9000
rules.evidence_template: MTU {twin_a}={a}, {twin_b}={b}; netplan mtu {np}.
rules.why_it_matters: Silent jumbo-frame drops; a 3-node NCCL failure and the 3 GB/s plateau were traced to 1500 vs 9000.
next_steps: mtu: 9000 on all twins on every node (switch l2mtu 9216); verify ping -M do -s 8972 <peer>.

rules.trigger: CX-7 twins Up AND (NCCL_IB_HCA names a netdev, lists one twin of a cage, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1, an NCCL net plugin present without NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none, libnccl.so.2 < 2.28, 3+ nodes without NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1, or a supplied log shows 'Using network Socket' / 'ibv_modify_qp failed with 110')
rules.evidence_template: NCCL_IB_HCA={hca}; NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME={ifname}; NCCL_IB_DISABLE={dis}; NCCL_NET_PLUGIN={plugin} (lib {lib}); libnccl {ver}; log '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Each misstep drops the pair from ~22-24 GB/s busbw to ~12 GB/s (one twin) or 1-3 GB/s (sockets); NCCL < 2.28 lacks sm_121 and hangs.
next_steps: export NCCL_IB_HCA=rocep1s0f1,roceP2p1s0f1 (both twins of the cabled port) NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<cabled netdev> NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3 NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none; rings: NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1 NCCL_IB_MERGE_NICS=0; build NCCL v2.30.7-1 with -gencode=arch=compute_121,code=sm_121; confirm 'NET/IB' in NCCL_DEBUG=INFO.

rules.trigger: NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL set (not 0/LOC) or NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE=1, or dmesg 'nvidia_peermem: Unknown symbol ib_register_peer_memory_client'
rules.evidence_template: {var}={value}; nvidia_peermem load attempted {attempted}. NCCL logs 'GPU Direct RDMA Disabled for HCA' / 'GDR 0' on Spark.
rules.why_it_matters: GPUDirect RDMA, nvidia-peermem, dma-buf and GDRCopy are unsupported (cudaMalloc memory is not CPU/PCIe coherent); assuming GDR causes init hangs.
next_steps: NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0, NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE=0; do not install nvidia-peermem/GDRCopy; RDMA buffers via cudaHostAlloc + ib_reg_mr.

rules.trigger: journalctl -u avahi-daemon 'Host name conflict, retrying with' or hostname with -2/-3 suffix; INFO variant when twins are Up but avahi-daemon/avahi-browse are absent
rules.evidence_template: avahi {state}: renamed host to {new_name} ('{line}'); avahi-utils {pkg}.
rules.why_it_matters: Cabled twins without DHCP flap and avahi sees its own announcements as conflicts; spark-xxxx.local becomes unreachable for NVIDIA Sync and discover-sparks needs avahi-browse.
next_steps: Static addresses on the twins (dhcp4: no); sudo apt-get install -y avahi-utils; sudo systemctl restart avahi-daemon.

rules.trigger: CX-7 twins addressed AND ufw enabled (/etc/ufw/ufw.conf ENABLED=yes) without allow rules for the fabric subnets or 5353/udp, 22/tcp, 29500/tcp
rules.evidence_template: ufw {state}, default {policy}; no rule for {missing} on {subnets}.
rules.why_it_matters: Blocks mDNS discovery, mpirun SSH launch and torch.distributed rendezvous ('Watchdog caught collective operation timeout').
next_steps: sudo ufw allow from <fabric-subnet>/24 (both twins) or at least 29500/tcp, 5353/udp, 22/tcp.

rules.trigger: RTX Spark AND (INF nv_surface_woa.inf OR driver 616.00 / WDDM 32.0.16.1600 OR package name DeveloperPreview OR driver < 616.00 on ARM64)
rules.evidence_template: Driver {version} ({inf}) is the RTX Spark Developer Preview branch (R616, 2026-07-16); below 616.00 on Arm64 is an extracted/unofficial build.
rules.why_it_matters: Preview issues: ~2 min blank display during install, GPU timeouts/restarts in PyTorch build workflows; not for production or benchmarking per NVIDIA.
next_steps: Check the RTX Spark Developer Preview thread and OEM/Windows Update for a production Arm64 driver.

rules.trigger: Windows ARM64 AND CUDA toolkit whose nvcc.exe PE machine is AMD64 (0x8664) or version <= 13.3
rules.evidence_template: CUDA {version} at {CUDA_PATH} is x86_64 under Prism; the first native Windows Arm64 toolkit is 13.4 Developer Preview.
rules.why_it_matters: An emulated toolkit targets x64 and cannot exercise the native Arm64 CUDA runtime.
next_steps: Install CUDA 13.4 DP (Windows ARM64) or cross-compile from x86_64; use pinned host memory (documented pageable slowdown).

rules.trigger: IsWow64Process2 native machine IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_ARM64 (0xAA64) AND process machine != IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_UNKNOWN
rules.evidence_template: NVCheckup runs under Prism (process {proc}, host ARM64); CPU data reflects the emulated processor.
rules.why_it_matters: Emulated processes get emulated CPU details and registry/filesystem redirection.
next_steps: Run nvcheckup-windows-arm64.exe.

rules.trigger: Windows ARM64 AND BuildNumber < 26100
rules.evidence_template: Windows build {build} predates 24H2 (26100); RTX Spark ships 26H1 (28000) or newer.
rules.why_it_matters: Prism AVX/AVX2 and downloadable Windows ML execution providers require 24H2+.
next_steps: Update to 24H2 or later (26H1 is device-scoped, not an in-place update).

rules.trigger: inside WSL2 AND dpkg/rpm lists nvidia-driver-* / nvidia-dkms-*, or /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so missing while the Windows driver is present
rules.evidence_template: WSL distro {distro} ({arch}) has Linux NVIDIA driver packages {pkgs}; /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so {present}.
rules.why_it_matters: CUDA in WSL comes from the Windows driver; NVIDIA: 'users must not install any NVIDIA GPU Linux driver within WSL 2'.
next_steps: Remove in-distro driver packages; update the Windows driver (>= 616.00 on RTX Spark); use aarch64 cu130 wheels in an aarch64 distro.

rules.trigger: Linux AND lspci [10de:2e03] or [10de:2e06]
rules.evidence_template: RTX Spark N1X [{pciid}] under Linux ({distro}, kernel {kernel}, driver {driver}); NVIDIA has announced no Linux support for RTX Spark.
rules.why_it_matters: Closest reference is DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04, R580 open, CUDA 13.0, sm_121); laptop drivers unverified.
next_steps: Treat results as best-effort; expect nvidia-smi memory fields [N/A] as on GB10.
